words.note: certainly 是 of course 很常見、較中性或稍正式的替代表達，可用來表示肯定、同意或確認某事是真的。
words.example: Certainly, I can send you the report this afternoon.
words.exampleZh: 當然可以，我今天下午可以把報告傳給你。

exercises.original: Of course, I can help you check the figures before the meeting.
exercises.zh: 當然可以，我可以在會議前幫你核對數字。
exercises.upgrade: certainly · 當然；確實；毫無疑問

options.explanation: certainly = 當然；可以。這裡是在直接答應幫忙，certainly 是自然、禮貌的肯定回應。
naturally = 自然地；理所當然地。通常表示事情符合常理，不如 certainly 適合直接答應請求。
unsurprisingly = 不出所料地。需要有可預測的結果，這裡不是在描述結果。
as expected = 正如預期。通常接結果或發展，不是直接答應幫忙。
needless to say = 不用說。用來引出顯而易見的陳述，不適合回應請求。
obviously = 顯然。若用來回應請求可能顯得不耐煩或帶評判意味。

exercises.original: “Can you keep this information confidential?” “Of course.”
exercises.zh: 「你可以把這些資料保密嗎？」「當然可以。」
exercises.upgrade: certainly · 當然；確實；毫無疑問

options.explanation: as expected = 正如預期。不能自然作為這種簡短答應。
certainly = 當然可以。作為對請求的簡短正式回應非常自然。
unsurprisingly = 不出所料。不是同意用語。
needless to say = 不用說。通常要接完整陳述。
naturally enough = 很自然地。不是最自然的單獨答應。
obviously = 顯然。語氣可能冒犯，像在說對方不應該問。

exercises.original: Of course, the final decision remains with the board.
exercises.zh: 當然，最終決定權仍然在董事會手上。
exercises.upgrade: certainly · 當然；確實；毫無疑問

options.explanation: certainly = 當然；確實。這裡是在強調一個明確、無疑的事實。
by chance = 偶然地。和肯定語氣不同。
perhaps = 或許。表示不確定，和 of course 相反。
apparently = 看來；據說。表示根據表面資訊推斷，沒有 certainly 那麼肯定。
possibly = 可能。表示機率，不是確認。
unexpectedly = 出乎意料地。與 of course 的自然／肯定感相反。

words.meaning: 自然地；理所當然地；當然
words.note: 當 of course 表示某事按照常理、情況或人的感受自然會如此時，可用 naturally。它重點是『這結果很自然』。
words.example: Naturally, she was nervous before her first performance.
words.exampleZh: 她第一次表演前緊張，當然是很自然的。

exercises.original: Of course, he was disappointed after missing the final by one point.
exercises.zh: 他只差一分未能進入決賽，感到失望當然很自然。
exercises.upgrade: naturally · 自然地；理所當然地；當然

options.explanation: naturally = 理所當然地。missing the final by one point 很自然會令人失望，最貼合因果和人之常情。
certainly = 確實。可以強調真實性，但不如 naturally 表達情緒反應是自然結果。
as expected = 正如預期。也接近，但較像外部預測，而不是人之常情。
needless to say = 不用說。語氣較修辭化，這裡不如 naturally 自然。
definitely = 肯定地。強調確定，不是自然結果。
sure = 當然／可以。較口語且常用於回應。

exercises.original: Of course, parents worry when their children travel alone for the first time.
exercises.zh: 孩子第一次獨自旅行時，父母會擔心是很自然的。
exercises.upgrade: naturally · 自然地；理所當然地；當然

options.explanation: certainly = 確實。語意可通，但沒有 naturally 那麼突出這是合乎人情的反應。
naturally = 理所當然地。parents worry + first time alone 是典型自然反應。
definitely = 肯定地。強調確定程度。
sure = 當然。可口語回應，但放在句首這裡不如 naturally 正式自然。
as expected by schedule = 按時間表預期。完全不合情緒語境。
needless to say = 不用說。較修辭化，語氣更強。

exercises.original: The room became noisy, of course, once fifty children arrived.
exercises.zh: 五十個孩子一到，房間當然很自然地變得嘈吵。
exercises.upgrade: naturally · 自然地；理所當然地；當然

options.explanation: naturally = 自然地；理所當然地。fifty children arriving 很自然會令房間變嘈吵。
perhaps = 也許。表示不確定，力度不合。
accidentally = 意外地。不是意外，而是可預期結果。
surprisingly = 令人驚訝地。方向相反。
apparently = 看來。只是根據表面判斷。
possibly = 可能地。不是確定的自然結果。

words.note: 當 of course 用於強烈確認、保證或表達明確立場時，可用 definitely。它比 certainly 更口語、更強調『肯定』。
words.example: I would definitely recommend this course.
words.exampleZh: 我一定會推薦這個課程。

exercises.original: “Would you visit the city again?” “Of course—I loved it.”
exercises.zh: 「你會再去這個城市嗎？」「當然會——我很喜歡那裡。」
exercises.upgrade: definitely · 一定；肯定；當然

options.explanation: definitely = 一定；當然。這裡是強烈、口語地表達明確意願。
naturally = 理所當然地。不是最自然的簡短回應。
as expected = 正如預期。不是回答意願。
unsurprisingly = 不出所料。不能自然單獨回答問題。
needless to say = 不用說。通常引出完整句。
apparently = 看來。反而表示不完全確定。

exercises.original: Of course I want to come; I've been looking forward to it all week.
exercises.zh: 我當然想來；我整個星期都很期待。
exercises.upgrade: definitely · 一定；肯定；當然

options.explanation: naturally only = 只表示理所當然。可理解，但 looking forward all week 更直接支持強烈意願。
definitely = 肯定。want to come + strong evidence of enthusiasm 很自然。
possibly = 可能。太不確定。
apparently = 看來。像是根據外部證據猜測自己的意願，不合。
perhaps = 或許。和強烈期待相反。
unexpectedly = 出乎意料地。無關。

exercises.original: Of course, this is the best option if we want the fastest result.
exercises.zh: 如果我們想最快得到結果，這當然是最佳選擇。
exercises.upgrade: definitely · 一定；肯定；當然

options.explanation: definitely = 肯定。best option + fastest result 是明確強調判斷。
maybe = 也許。過於不確定。
arguably only = 可以說。會降低肯定程度。
possibly = 可能。也太弱。
apparently = 看來。只是表面判斷。
by chance = 偶然。無關。

words.meaning: 不出所料地；毫不意外地
words.note: 當 of course 表示某個結果完全不令人意外，因為前文已有充分原因時，可用 unsurprisingly。它特別適合敘述結果。
words.example: Unsurprisingly, sales fell after the price increase.
words.exampleZh: 價格上升後，銷售下跌並不令人意外。

exercises.original: Of course, sales fell after the company doubled its prices.
exercises.zh: 公司把價格提高一倍後，銷售下跌當然不出所料。
exercises.upgrade: unsurprisingly · 不出所料地；毫不意外地

options.explanation: unsurprisingly = 不出所料地。doubled its prices 提供明確原因，sales fell 是可預測結果。
certainly = 確實。只強調真實，不如 unsurprisingly 突出結果不意外。
naturally as permission = 作為允許用語的 naturally 並不適合這個結果句。
definitely as a reply = 作為簡短回應的 definitely 不合句法功能。
needless to say = 不用說。也可表示顯然，但語氣更修辭化。
sure = 當然。太口語且不適合正式結果敘述。

exercises.original: The road was covered in ice, and of course several buses were delayed.
exercises.zh: 道路結冰，幾架巴士延誤當然毫不意外。
exercises.upgrade: unsurprisingly · 不出所料地；毫不意外地

options.explanation: as a favor = 作為幫忙。無關。
unsurprisingly = 不出所料地。ice on the road → delays 是清楚可預期結果。
certainly to agree = 用作答應的 certainly。這裡不是回應請求。
sure = 當然。過於口語，也不適合敘述結果。
naturally to grant permission = 表示允許的 naturally。語義不合。
needless to say only = 不用說。可能可用，但這題最自然的是 unsurprisingly。

exercises.original: The team had not trained for months, so of course they struggled in the first match.
exercises.zh: 球隊幾個月沒有訓練，所以首場比賽表現掙扎並不意外。
exercises.upgrade: unsurprisingly · 不出所料地；毫不意外地

options.explanation: unsurprisingly = 不出所料地。not trained for months 是足夠原因，struggled 是可預見結果。
possibly = 可能地。太不確定。
apparently = 看來。只是根據表面推測。
accidentally = 意外地。不是偶然行為。
unexpectedly = 出乎意料地。方向相反。
perhaps = 或許。力度太弱。

words.note: 當 of course 表示事情按照先前預測、計劃或合理預期發生時，可用 as expected。它比 naturally 更明確指向『先前已有預期』。
words.example: As expected, the train was crowded during rush hour.
words.exampleZh: 正如預期，繁忙時間的火車很擠迫。

exercises.original: Of course, the train was crowded during the evening rush hour.
exercises.zh: 正如預期，晚間繁忙時間的火車很擠迫。
exercises.upgrade: as expected · 正如預期；如所料

options.explanation: as expected = 正如預期。rush hour 提供先前可作出的合理預測。
certainly = 確實。沒有明確表達『之前已預料到』。
definitely = 肯定。強調確定程度，不是結果符合預測。
sure = 當然。過於口語。
needless to say = 不用說。較修辭化。
naturally as permission = 用作允許語氣的 naturally 不合。

exercises.original: The first test was difficult and, of course, the average score was lower than usual.
exercises.zh: 第一次測驗很難，正如預期，平均分比平常低。
exercises.upgrade: as expected · 正如預期；如所料

options.explanation: unsurprisingly only = 不出所料。也很接近，但這題目標是『符合預期結果』的較中性表達。
as expected = 正如預期。difficult test → lower average score 是自然預測關係。
certainly = 確實。缺少預測意味。
sure = 當然。語域太口語。
definitely as reply = 用作回答的 definitely。句法功能不合。
needless to say = 不用說。語氣較強、更修辭化。

exercises.original: Of course, demand increased once the price was cut by half.
exercises.zh: 價格減半後，需求正如預期般增加。
exercises.upgrade: as expected · 正如預期；如所料

options.explanation: as expected = 正如預期。price cut → demand increase 是明確可預測的商業結果。
perhaps = 或許。表示不確定。
unexpectedly = 出乎意料地。相反。
accidentally = 偶然地。不是此處語義。
apparently = 看來。只表示表面／聽說。
possibly = 可能。太弱。

words.note: 較修辭化的片語，用來引出說話者認為非常明顯、幾乎不必特別說明的事情。比一般 of course 更強，也較適合完整陳述。
words.example: Needless to say, everyone was relieved when the child was found.
words.exampleZh: 不用說，孩子被找到時大家都鬆了一口氣。

exercises.original: Of course, everyone was relieved when the missing child was found safe.
exercises.zh: 不用說，失蹤孩子安全找到時，所有人都鬆了一口氣。
exercises.upgrade: needless to say · 不用說；當然不用多說

options.explanation: needless to say = 不用說。everyone relieved after child found safe 是幾乎毋須解釋的明顯反應。
certainly = 確實。也可，但沒有 needless to say 的修辭效果。
sure = 當然。較口語，且不適合這種正式敘述開頭。
as expected by schedule = 按計劃預期。情緒反應不是時間表結果。
possibly = 可能。過於不確定。
apparently = 看來。也降低肯定程度。

exercises.original: Of course, the family was devastated by the loss of their home.
exercises.zh: 不用說，失去家園令這家人悲痛不已。
exercises.upgrade: needless to say · 不用說；當然不用多說

options.explanation: naturally only = 理所當然。可用，但 needless to say 更符合強烈、顯而易見的修辭陳述。
needless to say = 不用說。loss of home → devastation 是非常明顯的情緒結果。
definitely as permission = 用作允許語氣的 definitely 不合。
sure = 當然。太口語。
as expected by timetable = 按時間表預期。完全不合。
perhaps = 或許。與強烈明確情緒不符。

exercises.original: Of course, the company apologized after discovering that customers had been charged twice.
exercises.zh: 不用說，公司發現顧客被重複收費後作出了道歉。
exercises.upgrade: needless to say · 不用說；當然不用多說

options.explanation: needless to say = 不用說。serious billing error → apology 是說話者認為顯而易見的反應。
possibly = 可能。太弱。
unexpectedly = 出乎意料。方向相反。
by chance = 偶然。無關。
perhaps = 或許。降低確定程度。
apparently = 看來。像是未完全確認。

words.note: 在非正式對話中，sure 常用來代替 of course 回應請求、許可或邀請。它不適合所有陳述性 of course。
words.exampleZh: 「我可以借你的筆嗎？」「當然可以。」

exercises.original: “Can I sit here?” “Of course.”
exercises.zh: 「我可以坐這裡嗎？」「當然可以。」
exercises.upgrade: sure · 當然；可以（口語）

options.explanation: sure = 當然；可以。對簡單許可請求的口語回應非常自然。
as expected = 正如預期。不是許可回應。
unsurprisingly = 不出所料。無關。
naturally in a result sentence = 用來描述自然結果的 naturally。不是最自然的單獨口語許可。
needless to say = 不用說。不能自然單獨回答這種請求。
apparently = 看來。表示不確定。

exercises.original: “Would you mind sending me the link?” “Of course, no problem.”
exercises.zh: 「你介意把連結傳給我嗎？」「當然可以，沒問題。」
exercises.upgrade: sure · 當然；可以（口語）

options.explanation: certainly formally = 正式地 certainly。也能答應，但這句對話語氣很輕鬆，sure 更自然。
sure = 當然；可以。no problem 與 sure 是很自然的口語搭配。
as expected = 正如預期。無法回應請求。
unsurprisingly = 不出所料。無關。
needless to say = 不用說。不是簡短答應。
possibly = 可能。顯得不確定。

exercises.original: “Can you wait five minutes?” “Of course.”
exercises.zh: 「你可以等五分鐘嗎？」「當然可以。」
exercises.upgrade: sure · 當然；可以（口語）

options.explanation: sure = 當然；可以。這是簡單、自然的口語答應。
unexpectedly = 出乎意料地。無關。
perhaps = 或許。不是明確答應。
apparently = 看來。無關。
as expected = 正如預期。不是回應請求。
unsurprisingly = 不出所料。無關。

falseSynonyms.zh: 顯然；明顯地不等於一般的 of course obviously = 顯然；明顯地 obviously 有時和 of course 接近，但常帶『這很明顯，你應該知道』的語氣，對人說話時可能顯得不耐煩或居高臨下，因此不能普遍互換。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON “Of course I can help” is polite; “Obviously I can help” can sound dismissive.

falseSynonyms.zh: 很可能不等於一般的 of course probably = 很可能 probably 表示高機率但仍有不確定性；of course 通常表示肯定、自然或不出所料。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Probably means likely, not certain.

falseSynonyms.zh: 也許；或許不等於一般的 of course perhaps = 也許；或許 perhaps 明確表示不確定，通常和 of course 的肯定語氣相反。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Perhaps weakens certainty; of course strengthens it.

falseSynonyms.zh: 看來；據說不等於一般的 of course apparently = 看來；據說 apparently 表示根據表面證據或聽來的資訊作判斷，說話者未必完全確定。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Apparently signals some distance from certainty.

falseSynonyms.zh: 不可避免地不等於一般的 of course inevitably = 不可避免地 inevitably 表示某結果無法避免，力度比 of course 強很多；很多『當然』的事情並不是必然。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Expected is not always inevitable.

falseSynonyms.zh: 當然可以；儘管不等於一般的 of course by all means = 當然可以；儘管 by all means 可在授予許可時表示『當然可以』，但它只適合特定回應語境，不能替代敘述句中的 of course。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON “By all means, come in” works for permission, not for every use of of course.

falseSynonyms.zh: 課程；路線；過程不等於一般的 of course course = 課程；路線；過程 course 單獨是一個完全不同的名詞；of course 是固定片語，不能從字面拆開理解。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON A course can be a class or route; of course is an idiom.

falseSynonyms.zh: 錯誤拼法不等於一般的 of course ofcourse = 錯誤拼法 標準英文必須寫成兩個字：of course。ofcourse 不是標準拼法。
